description:
Upstream's StreamAC on the settings our kernel scored 1034.13 with, which is trial 4 of the 20-trial search (launch 20260727-201154) and within 1% of the 1043.66 the historical run recorded. One run, no search: the question is whether the two implementations behave alike over two million steps, and the block tests already say their arithmetic agrees to a fraction of a last bit.
Read the curve, not only the number. Our kernel's trial 4 climbed to its peak and held; a comparison that lands at a similar score by a different route is a different answer than one that tracks it. Both report eval/episode_return in the task's own units -- upstream normalises rewards in a wrapper, so this entry digs the paid reward back out rather than summing the scaled one.
Two differences are structural and are not being controlled for, because they are what upstream is: normalisation lives in wrappers whose statistics restart at every evaluation, and there is no credit choice, so this is our tbptt and not our rtrl.
name: ablate-upstream
